analysis: Integration pass over the SSD eviction refactor. The replayed source shows SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift, head lines ~12-33) probing index.oldest() first and retiring that tag. It returns 0 on externalChange and returns the freed bytes on success. Otherwise it iterates index.oldestFirstSnapshot() while skipping the first tag. SSDBlockIndex.swift (head lines ~167-225) replaces the sorted oldestEntries() with a min-heap snapshot. The heap sift-down and heapify are standard, and precedes is a total order because tags are unique. The snapshot is copied under the index lock, and retirement runs outside the lock, so there is no lock-held-across-I/O DoS. Both call sites (SSDPrefixCache.evictOldestEntry, SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.evictOldestEntry) keep the retireIndexedEntries([url]) closure. That keeps the removalLock, hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot checks, leases and epoch validation, and the externalChange reconciliation. The old semantics are preserved: it skips busy or undeletable victims, stops on external change, counts evictions only when bytes were freed, and the iteration is bounded. The earlier source passes' open question about helper semantics is resolved by the replayed helper source. The URLs are built from index-derived HMAC tags under config.root, so no new path input. No changes to crypto, HMAC naming, DBK3 AAD, the 1800s TTL, disk budget policy, epoch rotation or KEK purge, so the T-041 posture is unchanged. Docs and changelog are consistent with the code. Minor note: the snapshot is taken after the first attempt, so concurrent eviction schedules can choose different victims. That is a fairness matter only, not a security regression. Coverage limit: 36 replay units were omitted, including test files and SSDDiskBudget, which were not directly inspected. No findings.
